subject: Post-call notes: ops guardrails, SLO targets & hybrid VPC topology
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Elena Martinez <elena@meditect.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: ops guardrails, SLO targets & hybrid VPC topology

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap + agreed next steps so we have the same action items captured. I focused on the operational guarantees and the hybrid deployment options since those were the highest priority for your infra and security teams.

What we heard
- Primary pain: inconsistent inference latency under spiky traffic for clinical NLP batch jobs (30–120 req/min bursts) and a concern about PHI touching hosted environments.
- Primary goal: predictable P95 latency <= 350ms for text-classification endpoints at sustained 50 req/min and graceful tail behavior for spikes to 150 req/min.
- Minimum model requirement: fine-tuned medical NER + classification (LLaMA-2 family equivalent) with 8k context and KV cache support.

Key technical notes we discussed
- Topology: hybrid deployment — control plane on Redwood hosted, inference in your VPC via private nodes (we demonstrated same API surface, routing to private model workers).
- Batching: continuous batching with per-customer burst cap and conservative max batch latency (we suggested max 60ms batch delay).
- Caching: prefix/KV cache for session-based work; recommendation to enable per-route caching for long-running flows.
- Quantization: we proposed INT8 for the classifier and FP16 for the NER head in the model-profile to keep throughput high without accuracy regressions.
- Fallbacks: automated routing to a smaller quantized variant if warm capacity is exhausted.

Operational SLOs we sketched (agreeable to iterate)
- P95 token generation latency <= 350ms at steady-state 50 req/min
- P99 tail <= 900ms under spikes up to 150 req/min with autoscale/burst policy enabled
- Availability goal: 99.9% for production inference endpoints (SLA conversation to follow)

Action items / next steps
1) Meditect -> share the full prod traffic profile (per-endpoint QPS distribution + sample traces) (Elena).
2) Redwood -> run a sizing sketch and provide expected node count and cost delta for hybrid VPC path (Irene + Karthik) — aiming to send the first draft by EOD Thu.
3) Security -> sample SOC2 artifact and network diagram for VPC peering/hops (Vivek) — add to shared Drive.
4) Schedule: deep technical session with your infra + security next Tue (I'll propose times).

Attachments: I attached a brief MOP for hybrid deployments and asked for the latency profile template in the drive.

Thanks — I think we have a clear path to a scoped POC.

—
Irene Choi
Senior Solutions Engineer\Redwood Inference
irene@redwood.com

From: Elena Martinez <elena@meditect.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 10:07:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: ops guardrails, SLO targets & hybrid VPC topology

Irene — thanks for the thorough summary. Quick confirmations and one clarification below.

Confirmations
- We'll export the QPS distribution and a 48h trace window for the endpoints you highlighted (classification + NER). Expect that in a shared Drive folder by EOD Wednesday.
- P95 target of 350ms aligns with product expectations; we'll need a short validation run against our dev dataset to confirm model latency with INT8/FP16 profiles.

Clarification
- For "spikes to 150 req/min" — those are short bursts (90–120s) rather than sustained. The P99 tail expectation is most important for our on-call SLA.

Request
- Can your sizing sketch include expected cold-start behavior (first response on an idle worker) and an estimated warmup token cost? We'll use that to size our cost buckets.

Attachments: I uploaded a starter latency profile (meditect_latency_profile.xlsx) to the Drive link you shared.

Appreciate the quick follow-up. I'll await your sizing sketch and will coordinate the infra + security attendees for the deep dive next week.

—
Elena Martinez
Head of Platform Engineering\Meditect
elena@meditect.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Martinez <elena@meditect.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 13:28:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: ops guardrails, SLO targets & hybrid VPC topology

Elena / Irene — a couple of technical clarifications from the sizing perspective:

1) Model variants: we'll propose two runtime variants in the sketch — (A) quantized INT8 classifier + FP16 NER (preferred for cost/throughput) and (B) fully FP16 baseline for comparison. Please flag if your validation run prefers another quant profile.

2) Autoscale and burst: our proposal will include a burst provisioning policy that keeps a small warm pool per-region and allows short duration extra capacity via pre-warmed nodes. For the initial sketch I need the expected concurrency per endpoint and percent of requests that require the NER path vs. classification-only.

3) Cold start: rough numbers — cold-start first-token latency for a fresh worker (8xA100-equivalent) should be ~1.1–1.6s depending on KV load; warm steady-state p95 for the same hardware is what we'll target under 350ms. I'll put exact ranges in the sketch.

I've attached a short MOP extract we use for hybrid VPC connectivity (redwood_mop_brief.pdf) — it contains network port requirements and the peering handshake steps.

I'll draft the sizing doc and a quick cost delta estimate. Irene — can you take lead on shareable artifacts and schedule the Tuesday deep-dive?

Thanks,
Karthik
Principal Solutions Architect\Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Elena Martinez <elena@meditect.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 17:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: ops guardrails, SLO targets & hybrid VPC topology

All — thanks for the rapid turns. Finalizing next steps and timeline below so Meditect and Redwood teams are aligned.

Immediate deliverables (this week)
- Meditect: QPS distribution + 48h traces (Elena) — drop in Drive by Wed EOD.
- Redwood: Sizing sketch + cost delta + cold-start profiles (Karthik + Irene) — initial draft by Thu EOD.
- Redwood Security: sample SOC2 excerpt + VPC peering diagram (Vivek) — upload by Thu.

Deep dive session
- Proposed window: Tue 2027-01-19 10:00–11:30 PT. Agenda: traffic profile review (15m), sizing sketch walk-through (25m), network/security constraints (20m), validation plan + next-phase POC scope (30m).
- Please confirm availability; I'll send a calendar invite and include an agenda doc + HubSpot link (HS-48291).

Acceptance criteria for POC (draft)
- P95 latency <= 350ms for classification at 50 req/min sustained in hybrid VPC deployment using proposed model variant A.
- Health check: end-to-end tracing enabled and ingestion into your APM (we'll provide a tracing hook example).
- Security: no PHI persisted in Redwood logs; audit events forwarded to your KMS/HSM.

If that looks good I'll send the invite and attach the draft sketch as soon as it's ready.

Thanks — looking forward to the deep dive.

—
Irene Choi
Senior Solutions Engineer\Redwood Inference
irene@redwood.com

On a separate note: Elena, small ask — if you can include a couple of sample payloads that represent worst-case token length that will help us size sequence length and KV cache requirements.
